classification.difficultyReason: Three linked practical models:openpool surface tiling, difference-of-rectangles border and reduced-depth volume/flow; explicit scaffolding bounds strategy demand.

content.prompt: A swimming pool is in the shape of a rectangular prism. The pool is 12 m long, 4 m wide and 1.5 m deep. The pool is to be lined with tiles.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many tiles are needed to line the pool if each tile is $200\text{ mm}\times200\text{ mm}$?

answer.worked:
The open pool has a floor and four walls. Each tile has area $0.2^2=0.04\text{ m}^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=12\times4+2(12\times1.5)+2(4\times1.5)\\A&=96\text{ m}^2\\\text{Tiles}&=96\div0.04=2400.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A path 1 m wide is to be laid around the pool. How many pavers are needed to make the path if the size of each of the pavers is $500\text{ mm}\times500\text{ mm}$?

answer.worked:
The outside dimensions are 14 m by 6 m. Each paver has area $0.5^2=0.25\text{ m}^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{path}}&=14\times6-12\times4=36\text{ m}^2\\\text{Pavers}&=36\div0.25=144.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: When the pool is completed, it is filled at 400 L/h. How long will it take to fill the pool to 10 cm below the top?

answer.worked:
The water depth is $1.5-0.1=1.4$ m.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=12\times4\times1.4=67.2\text{ m}^3\\V&=67200\text{ L}\\t&=67200\div400=168\text{ hours}.\end{aligned}$$
